title: Scientific Discoveries
tagline: Milestones that changed how we see the world.
source: Generated from “Timeline of scientific discoveries” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Supernova Cosmology Project
events.text: Supernova Cosmology Project and the High-Z Supernova Search Team: discovery of the accelerated expansion of the Universe and dark energy

events.title: Tau neutrino
events.text: The Tau neutrino is discovered by the DONUT collaboration

events.title: Vela
events.text: Vela nuclear test detection satellites discover the first gamma-ray burst

events.title: Multiplication tables in a base-60, rather than base-10 (decimal), sys
events.text: Multiplication tables in a base-60, rather than base-10 (decimal), system from Babylon.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of scientific discoveries

events.title: Babylonian cuneiform numerals
events.text: Primitive positional notation for numerals is seen in the Babylonian cuneiform numerals. However, the lack of clarity around the notion of zero made their system highly ambiguous (e.g. would be written the same as ).

events.title: Berlin Papyrus 6619
events.text: Pythagorean triples are first discussed in Babylon and Egypt, and appear on later manuscripts such as the Berlin Papyrus 6619.

events.title: Human Genome Project
events.text: The first draft of the Human Genome Project is published.

events.title: Raymond Davis Jr.
events.text: – Raymond Davis Jr. and Masatoshi Koshiba detect transformations of different types of neutrinos, demonstrating that they have mass.

events.title: Grigori Perelman
events.text: Grigori Perelman presents proof of the Poincaré Conjecture.

events.title: The Human Genome Project sequences the human genome with a 92% accurac
events.text: The Human Genome Project sequences the human genome with a 92% accuracy.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of scientific discoveries

events.title: Andre Geim
events.text: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov isolated graphene, a monolayer of carbon atoms, and studied its quantum electrical properties.

events.title: Ben Green
events.text: Ben Green and Terence Tao announce their proof on arithmetic progressions in prime numbers known as the Green–Tao Theorem.

events.title: Grid cells
events.text: Grid cells in the brain are discovered by Edvard Moser and May-Britt Moser.

events.title: The first self-replicating, synthetic bacterial cells are constructed
events.text: The first self-replicating, synthetic bacterial cells are constructed.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of scientific discoveries

events.title: Neanderthal Genome Project
events.text: The Neanderthal Genome Project presented preliminary genetic evidence that interbreeding likely occurred and that a small but significant portion of Neanderthal admixture is present in modern non-African populations.

events.title: Higgs boson
events.text: Higgs boson is discovered at CERN (confirmed to 99.999% certainty)

events.title: Photonic molecule
events.text: Photonic molecules are discovered at MIT

events.title: Exotic hadron
events.text: Exotic hadrons are discovered at the LHCb

events.title: Photonic metamaterial
events.text: Photonic metamaterials are discovered to make passive daytime radiative cooling possible by Raman et al.

events.title: LIGO
events.text: The LIGO team detects gravitational waves from a black hole merger

events.title: GW170817
events.text: Gravitational wave signal GW170817 is observed by the LIGO/Virgo collaboration. This is the first instance of a gravitational wave event observed to have a simultaneous electromagnetic signal when space telescopes like Hubble observed lights coming f

events.title: first image of a black hole is captured
events.text: The first image of a black hole is captured, using eight different telescopes taking simultaneous pictures, timed with extremely precise atomic clocks.

references.label: first image of a black hole is captured

events.title: NASA
events.text: NASA and SOFIA (Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy) discover about 350 mL of surface water in one of the Moon's largest visible craters.

events.title: human genome
events.text: The standard reference gene, GRCh38.p14, of the human genome, is fully sequenced and contains 3.1 billion base pairs.

events.title: Quadratic equations
events.text: Quadratic equations, in the form of problems relating the areas and sides of rectangles, are solved by Babylonians.

events.title: area
events.text: The concept of area is first recognized in Babylonian clay tablets, and 3-dimensional volume is discussed in an Egyptian papyrus. This begins the study of geometry.
